record.paper_title: Time and Norm Optimal Controls: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Construct a hypersingular time-optimal control in a space where time-optimal controls are unique, for example in a Hilbert space. Here hypersingularity means that the time-optimal control remains strongly singular on every subinterval [α, β] with 0 ≤ α < β ≤ T, rather than merely failing the maximum principle on the whole control interval. The paper gives hypersingular examples only in the very rough space c_0, where uniqueness of time-optimal controls fails, so the open problem is to obtain such an example in a setting with uniqueness.

evidence.quote: It would obviously be better to have an example of an hypersingular control in a space where uniqueness of time optimal controls holds (e.g. a Hilbert space) but we don’t know of any.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $U \subset X$ be the closed unit ball. Consider a linear control system
$$\dot y(t) = A y(t) + u(t), \qquad y(0)=y_0,$$
where $A$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup on $X$ (or, in the finite-dimensional analogue, $A$ is a bounded operator on $X$) and the admissible controls are measurable functions $u:[0,T]\to U$. Given a target $y_1\in X$ reachable from $y_0$, a time-optimal control is an admissible $u^*$ defined on $[0,T^*]$, with $T^*$ the minimal time at which $y_1$ is reachable, that steers $y_0$ to $y_1$.

A time-optimal control $u^*$ is said to satisfy the Pontryagin maximum principle on a subinterval $[\alpha,\beta]\subset[0,T^*]$ if there exists a nonzero functional $\xi\in X^*$ such that for almost every $t\in[\alpha,\beta]$,
$$\langle \xi, e^{(T^*-t)A^*} u^*(t)\rangle = \sup_{v\in U}\langle \xi, e^{(T^*-t)A^*} v\rangle.$$
The control $u^*$ is called strongly singular on $[\alpha,\beta]$ if the maximum principle fails on $[\alpha,\beta]$. The control $u^*$ is called hypersingular if it is strongly singular on every subinterval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $0\le \alpha<\beta\le T^*$.

It is known that in the space $X=c_0$ hypersingular time-optimal controls exist, but uniqueness of time-optimal controls fails there. It is also known that in a Hilbert space (and more generally in strictly convex reflexive spaces) time-optimal controls, when they exist, are unique.

Problem. Construct a linear control system on a Hilbert space $X$ (or more generally on a Banach space in which time-optimal controls are unique) which admits a hypersingular time-optimal control, or else prove that no such example exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any construction of a hypersingular time-optimal control in a Hilbert space or in any setting where time-optimal controls are unique. The known hypersingular examples remain confined to rough spaces such as $c_0$ where uniqueness fails, so the question appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Optimal Control in Hilbert Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and uniqueness results for optimal control in Hilbert spaces for exactly controllable linear systems.
status_evidence.claim: Standard uniqueness results for time-optimal controls in Hilbert spaces are well established, but no hypersingular example in such settings is reported.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert Uniqueness Method (HUM)
status_evidence.snippet: HUM connects null controllability with exact observability and yields unique controls via Hilbert space optimization.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of controls in Hilbert space settings is well-documented; no hypersingular counterpart is identified.
